text: rwb-source-data extracts the partner, partner_user and partner_instruction rows of the open cases at cutover and hands them to rwb-partner as one package per cutover business date; S9 loads them into rwb_partner on S9's own Flyway sequence, and P1 holds no INSERT, no join and no read against that schema. The AC3 Given is proved against the rwb-partner contract mock until S9's load exists.
why: The Ownership Map gives the three tables to S9 while the legacy key is a P1 migration story, and DP-01 forbids a service writing another service's tables; the handover is the only shape that keeps both rules, and AC3 can then be proved without waiting for the live load.
read: Ownership Map v1 (P1 and S9 rows); TSD P1 v3 T3.6; Architecture v5 slides 29, 41 and 45; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-01 and DP-15; CG-B2-P1-007-2
confirm: Solution architect with the S9 owner in the cutover rehearsal and the baseline review of the P1 contract story.
impact: If S9 loads the rows itself at another point or through another path, one handover step, the rwb-partner mock and two fixtures change; no table, event or workflow of P1 changes.

text: The partner_instruction overlap between RWB-DM-008 and RWB-DM-007 is split by content: this key hands over the panel, the partner users and the performance facts of every instruction (case, type, instructed_at, due_at, result), RWB-DM-007 hands over the instructions raised for legal actions, both packages carry the same instruction id, and S9 writes each id once by update rather than a second insert.
why: Both legacy keys name partner_instruction and the same field range, and no source rules which key owns which row; without a rule the same instruction reaches rwb_partner twice and the idempotent load cannot be built.
read: Legacy stories RWB-DM-007 and RWB-DM-008 (data rows DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016); FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 DP08; CG-B2-P1-007-1
confirm: Data steward with the RWB-DM-007 owner at the cutover rehearsal.
impact: If the ruling changes, one selector, one fixture and the package content of both keys change; no schema, event or contract change.

text: A clean day is a business date after the load for which the reconciliation_result rows written by JOB-04 carry no unexplained variance and no new REC-05 orphan on a key handed over by this cutover; a break row or a new orphan resets the count to zero and names the day, and the sign-off is recorded in the cutover record of the release pipeline only at ten consecutive clean days.
why: AC3 fixes the outcome of ten clean days but no source defines a clean day, where the count is held or what a break does, so the story cannot be built or tested without a rule.
read: RWB-DM-008 AC3; FSD P1 v3 A2.11.2 (REC-01, REC-02, REC-05) and A2.13; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 (reconciliation_result); DL25; CG-B2-P1-007-1
confirm: Data steward and the reconciliation owner in the cutover rehearsal, and RW-AUDIT for the evidence trail.
impact: If a clean day is defined another way, one evidence reader and one fixture change; the schema, the events and the contract are unaffected.

text: DP08 keeps the Workbench as its system of record with no ACE view and refresh ON_CHANGE, so this key reads no v_ace_* view, writes no data_product_load row for DP08 and carries no ACE freshness stamp; the recency evidence for the migrated partner rows is the daily reconciliation of the product, and MSG-P1-001 is asserted on the source product the day depends on and never as a DP08 stamp.
why: The data product catalog gives DP08 no ACE source and the freshness rules are written for source-fed products only, so a story that waited for an ACE batch or stamped a LOADED row would either wait forever or invent a provenance the product does not have.
read: FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 DP08 row; TSD P1 v3 T3.7 and T3.6 (data_product_load); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-05; CG-B2-P1-007-2
confirm: Data steward and the data product owner at the catalog review of DP08.
impact: If DP08 later gains an ACE source or a refresh rule, one freshness read and its test are added; nothing else in the story changes.

text: The cutover runs as one-off bulk work from the release pipeline for one business date, is started and read through this service's own admin operations (API-P1-002 and the data-quality exceptions read), and keeps its package and its evidence in the pipeline's cutover record rather than in a table; the dump's layout, the record's format and the retention window are pipeline configuration, agreed at the cutover rehearsal.
why: AC3 names a sign-off and a read-only window but no source fixes the step, the record or the dump, and the story must not invent a table or a workflow to hold them.
read: RWB-DM-008 endpoints row; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 32 and 44; TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A (API-P1-002); CG-B2-P1-007-1
confirm: DevOps lead and the solution architect at the cutover rehearsal.
impact: If the pipeline keeps the record elsewhere, one reader and one runbook line change; the schema, the contract and the events are unaffected.

text: The cutover extract is guarded by the platform feature flag rwb.source-data.dm008-cutover-extract: off, the step refuses to start and no package leaves, while this story's Flyway version still applies because it creates no table, no column and no index.
why: No source names a flag for a cutover slice, but the story needs a way to hold the step until S9's load and JOB-04's rows exist without holding a no-op migration.
read: Template and Rules R3 default ruling (feature flags, platform library); the flag pattern of the sibling P1 stories; CG-B2-P1-007-1
confirm: TechX lead and the platform flag owner at the story review.
impact: If the flag library names it another way, one values-file key and one test fixture change; no code path and no contract change.

text: RWB-DM-008 AC1 Extract the Workbench records and AC2 Reconcile the business keys are owned by RWB-ITG-DM008-ITG, which proves the extraction and the REC-05 business-key resolution across the services and carries TC-DM-008-01-ITG and TC-DM-008-02-ITG; this story keeps AC3 with TC-DM-008-03 and TC-DM-008-04 and proves its own extract, mapper and handover through the end-to-end fixture.
why: The split puts the cross-service proof with the harness, and the story cannot claim AC1 and AC2 without claiming the S9 and P3 behaviour it does not own.
read: RWB-ITG-DM008-ITG section 7 and 16; legacy RWB-DM-008 acceptance criteria and test case table; CG-B2-P1-007-1
confirm: Solution architect with the integration harness owner before the wave 4 harness run.
impact: If the harness leaves a criterion with this story, one criterion and one test case are added here and the same pair is removed from the harness.

text: The story stays at Status Draft (realignment v1): no approval of the split of RWB-DM-008 is recorded, and this run takes no approval step, so the status records the realignment and not a portfolio decision.
why: The realignment overlay of D-RCV-60 requires missing approvals and statuses to be recorded as assumptions and the work continued in Draft.
read: AGENTS.md rules 9 and 10 (realignment run rules); Template and Rules R1 U8; WP B2-P1-007
applied_in: RWB-P1-DM008-APP metadata row Status and the Status note under the metadata table
confirm: Portfolio owner at the realignment review after the stage.
impact: If the split is not approved, the story is re-cut or withdrawn and the P1 extract, the handover and the evidence reader leave with it; no other story changes.
